## Claude Managed Agents pricing

[Claude Managed Agents](https://platform.claude.com/docs/en/managed-agents/overview) is billed on two dimensions: tokens and session runtime.

### Tokens

All tokens consumed by a Claude Managed Agents session are billed at the rates shown in [Model pricing](https://platform.claude.com/docs/en/about-claude/pricing#model-pricing). [Prompt caching](https://platform.claude.com/docs/en/about-claude/pricing#prompt-caching) multipliers apply identically. Web search triggered inside a session incurs the standard $10 per 1,000 searches. On [Claude Platform on AWS](https://platform.claude.com/docs/en/about-claude/pricing#claude-platform-on-aws-pricing), session token and runtime charges convert to Claude Consumption Units at the standard rate. [Fast mode](https://platform.claude.com/docs/en/about-claude/pricing#fast-mode-pricing) premium pricing applies when an agent's `model.speed` is set to `"fast"`.

The [data residency multiplier](https://platform.claude.com/docs/en/about-claude/pricing#data-residency-pricing) also applies: when an agent's `model.inference_geo` is pinned to `"us"`, tokens consumed by sessions running that agent are billed at 1.1x the standard rates, the same multiplier that applies to US-only inference on the Messages API.

The following Messages API modifiers do **not** apply to Claude Managed Agents sessions:

| Modifier                                                                                                  | Why it doesn't apply                                           |
| --------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- | -------------------------------------------------------------- |
| [Batch API discount](https://platform.claude.com/docs/en/about-claude/pricing#batch-processing)           | Sessions are stateful and interactive. There is no batch mode. |
| [Cloud platform pricing](https://platform.claude.com/docs/en/about-claude/pricing#cloud-platform-pricing) | Not available on partner-operated cloud platforms.             |

### Session runtime

| SKU             | Rate                   | Metering                  |
| --------------- | ---------------------- | ------------------------- |
| Session runtime | $0.08 per session-hour | `running` status duration |

Runtime is measured to the millisecond and accrues only while the session's status is `running`. Time spent `idle` (waiting for your next message or a tool confirmation), `rescheduling`, or `terminated` does not count toward runtime.

<Note>
  Session runtime replaces the [code execution](https://platform.claude.com/docs/en/about-claude/pricing#code-execution-tool) container-hour billing model when using Claude Managed Agents. You are not separately billed for container hours on top of session runtime.
</Note>

### Worked example

A one-hour coding session using Claude Opus 5 that consumes 50,000 input tokens and 15,000 output tokens:

| Line item       | Calculation              | Cost       |
| --------------- | ------------------------ | ---------- |
| Input tokens    | 50,000 × $5 / 1,000,000  | $0.25      |
| Output tokens   | 15,000 × $25 / 1,000,000 | $0.375     |
| Session runtime | 1.0 hour × $0.08         | $0.08      |
| **Total**       |                          | **$0.705** |

If prompt caching is active and 40,000 of the input tokens are cache reads:

| Line item             | Calculation                   | Cost       |
| --------------------- | ----------------------------- | ---------- |
| Uncached input tokens | 10,000 × $5 / 1,000,000       | $0.05      |
| Cache read tokens     | 40,000 × $5 × 0.1 / 1,000,000 | $0.02      |
| Output tokens         | 15,000 × $25 / 1,000,000      | $0.375     |
| Session runtime       | 1.0 hour × $0.08              | $0.08      |
| **Total**             |                               | **$0.525** |

## Additional pricing considerations

### Cost optimization strategies

When building agents with Claude:

1. **Use appropriate models:** Choose Haiku for simple tasks, Sonnet for most production workloads, and Opus for the most complex reasoning
2. **Implement prompt caching:** Reduce costs for repeated context
3. **Batch operations:** Use the Batch API for non-time-sensitive tasks
4. **Monitor usage patterns:** Track token consumption to identify optimization opportunities

<Tip>
  For high-volume agent applications, contact the [enterprise sales team](https://claude.com/contact-sales) for custom pricing arrangements.
</Tip>

### Rate limits

Rate limits vary by usage tier and affect how many requests you can make:

* **Start tier:** Entry-level limits for getting started
* **Build tier:** Increased limits for growing applications
* **Scale tier:** Highest standard limits for production workloads

For detailed rate limit information, see [Rate limits](https://platform.claude.com/docs/en/api/rate-limits).

For limits beyond the Scale tier or custom pricing arrangements, [contact the sales team](https://claude.com/contact-sales).

### Volume discounts

Volume discounts may be available for high-volume users. These are negotiated on a case-by-case basis.

* Standard usage tiers use the pricing shown in [Model pricing](https://platform.claude.com/docs/en/about-claude/pricing#model-pricing)
* Enterprise customers can [contact sales](mailto:sales@anthropic.com) for custom pricing
* Academic and research discounts may be available

### Enterprise pricing

For enterprise customers with specific needs:

* Custom rate limits
* Volume discounts
* Dedicated support
* Custom terms

Contact the sales team at [sales@anthropic.com](mailto:sales@anthropic.com) or through the [Claude Console](https://platform.claude.com/usage/limits) to discuss enterprise pricing options.

## Billing and payment

* Billing is based on actual monthly usage
* All payments are in USD
* Credit card and invoicing options available
* Usage tracking available in the [Claude Console](https://platform.claude.com/)

## Frequently asked questions

### How is token usage calculated?

Tokens are pieces of text that models process. How many tokens the same text produces depends on the model's tokenizer, the language, and the type of content. Claude 4.7 and later models and Claude Mythos Preview use a newer tokenizer that produces approximately 30 percent more tokens for the same text than earlier models. To see how many tokens a request uses on a specific model, count it with [token counting](https://platform.claude.com/docs/en/build-with-claude/token-counting) and that model's ID.

### Are there free tiers or trials?

New users receive a small amount of free credits to test the API. [Contact sales](mailto:sales@anthropic.com) for information about extended trials for enterprise evaluation.

### How do discounts stack?

Batch API and prompt caching discounts can be combined. For example, using both features together provides significant cost savings compared to standard API calls. See [prompt caching pricing](https://platform.claude.com/docs/en/about-claude/pricing#prompt-caching) for how the multipliers interact.

### What payment methods are accepted?

Major credit cards are accepted for standard accounts. Enterprise customers can arrange invoicing and other payment methods.

For additional questions about pricing, contact [support@anthropic.com](mailto:support@anthropic.com).

# Gemini 2.5 Pricing Comparison

## Gemini 2.5 Flash

**Free Tier:** "Free of charge" for standard input and output

**Paid Tier (Standard):**
- Input: "$0.30 (text / image / video)" and "$1.00 (audio)"
- Output: "$2.50" per million tokens

## Gemini 2.5 Pro

**Free Tier:** "Free of charge" for standard input and output

**Paid Tier (Standard):**
- Input: "$1.25, prompts <= 200k tokens" and "$2.50, prompts > 200k tokens"
- Output: "$10.00, prompts <= 200k tokens" and "$15.00, prompts > 200k"

The Pro model charges at roughly 4-5x the rate of Flash, reflecting its enhanced reasoning capabilities for complex tasks.

1	export const SYSTEM_PROMPT = `You are Greenlight, an autonomous agent that fixes a failing test suite and nothing else.
2	
3	You will be given the output of a failing test run in a repository. Your job:
4	1. Call graph_search with a short plain-language description of the failure to find the likely fix site. This is backed by a real code graph (Entire) -- prefer it over guessing which file to open.

# Greenlight

> An autonomous agent that takes a repo with a failing test suite / red CI run, figures out why, writes a fix, verifies it, and opens a pull request — no human in the loop.

Built for [neatHack](https://neatlogs.com/hackathon) (Oct 10–12, 2026).

## Status

🚧 Under active development during the hackathon. See [`hackathon.md`](./hackathon.md) for the build log and evidence checklist.

## What it does

1. Point Greenlight at a repo with a failing test command (or a red GitHub Actions run).
2. It reproduces the failure, locates the relevant code via [Entire](https://entire.io)'s code graph, forms a hypothesis, and patches it.
3. It verifies: originally-failing tests pass, the full suite has no new failures, and no tests were deleted/skipped to "cheat" the fix.
4. If verification fails, it retries with a new hypothesis (up to a budget), recovering from tool errors, timeouts, and regressions along the way.
5. On success, it opens a PR with a summary of the root cause, the fix, and the evidence.

Every run is traced end-to-end in [neatlogs](https://neatlogs.com).

## Stack

- TypeScript / Node.js 20+
- Anthropic SDK (agent loop + tool use), traced via the neatlogs TypeScript SDK
- [Entire](https://entire.io) for build checkpoints and the `entire-graph` runtime code graph
- [cfo.ai](https://cfo.ai) for the business plan (see `evidence/`)

## Quickstart

```bash
npm install
cp .env.example .env   # fill in ANTHROPIC_API_KEY, NEATLOGS_API_KEY, GITHUB_TOKEN
npm run dev -- run --repo <path-to-repo> --test "npm test"
```

## Project layout

```
src/        agent loop, tools, tracing, recovery, verification
bench/      seeded buggy repos + benchmark runner
evidence/   traces, before/after numbers, business plan, screenshots
hackathon.md  dated build log + submission evidence checklist
```

## Evidence

See [`hackathon.md`](./hackathon.md) for links to traces, benchmark results, and the business plan.

# Greenlight — neatHack build log

## Project

**Name:** Greenlight
**One-sentence purpose:** An autonomous agent that turns a red CI run into a merged-ready pull request, with no human in the loop.
**Problem:** Engineers lose time triaging and fixing routine test failures; Greenlight handles the reproduce → locate → patch → verify → recover loop end to end.

## Team

- zoro (solo, so far)

## Stack

- TypeScript / Node.js 20+, Anthropic SDK
- neatlogs (tracing) — TS SDK
- Entire (build checkpoints) + entire-graph (runtime code graph)
- cfo.ai (business plan)
- GitHub Actions + Octokit (real red-CI → PR demo)

## Build log

### 2026-10-11 — M0: Setup
- Repo initialized, public GitHub repo created under `ivedmohan`.
- Entire CLI 0.11.4 installed via Homebrew; `entire enable` + `entire login` pending (human step).
- Neatlogs API key wired into `.env` (gitignored); project ID `73ddd324-c4e6-48fd-8667-2db6335ae52d`.
- Project scaffolded: `src/` (agent, tools, tracing), `bench/`, `evidence/`.
- Noted doc discrepancies vs. the original build brief:
  - Entire checkpoints are git refs at `refs/entire/checkpoints/<shard>/<id>` (linked via `Entire-Checkpoint` commit trailer), not a `entire/checkpoints/v1` branch.
  - entire-graph's search command is `entire graph query "<text>"`, not `entire graph search`. Setup is `entire graph init-agents --repo .` then `entire graph index`.

- `entire login` completed (human step); `entire auth status` confirms logged in as `github:ivedmohan`, checkpoints syncing to `origin`.

### 2026-10-11 — M1: Benchmark repos
- Built two golden seed projects under `bench/repos/`:
  - `stringkit` — TS utility library (capitalize, slugify, truncate, sum/clamp, array helpers, deepEqual, merge, retryWithBackoff). 8 test files, 36/36 tests passing.
  - `tasks-api` — tiny Express CRUD API for tasks, tested with supertest. 1 test file, 13/13 tests passing.
- Seeded 10 bug cases under `bench/cases/<project>/<id>/` (a `bug.patch` unified diff + `meta.json` with the difficulty and the *observed*, not assumed, failing tests):
  - `easy-capitalize` (stringkit) — `slice(0)` vs `slice(1)` duplicates the first char.
  - `easy-clamp` (stringkit) — off-by-one at the max boundary.
  - `easy-sum` (stringkit) — reduce starts at 1 instead of 0.
  - `medium-slugify-shared-helper` (stringkit) — bug is in `internal/normalize.ts`, not `slugify.ts`.
  - `medium-retry-missing-await` (stringkit) — missing `await` breaks error handling in `retryWithBackoff`.
  - `hard-shared-isplainobject` (stringkit) — one shared-helper bug breaks two unrelated test files at once (`compare.test.ts` + `merge.test.ts`); fix must go in the shared helper.
  - `flaky-retry-backoff-explosion` (stringkit) — backoff formula explodes, causing genuine test **timeouts** (verified at `--testTimeout=3000`, all 3 tests time out), not just wrong assertions.
  - `easy-completed-filter` (tasks-api) — query-string boolean not coerced before filtering.
  - `medium-update-store-bug` (tasks-api) — `updateTask()` returns a non-persisted copy; route code is correct, bug is cross-file.
  - `hard-validate-partial-flag-ignored` (tasks-api) — shared validation ignores the `partial` flag, breaking PATCH while CREATE still needs the required-title check; fix must be conditional.
- Wrote `bench/run-bench.ts`: for every case, copies the golden project, applies its patch, runs the real test suite, and checks observed failing test files against `meta.json`. **Ran it: 10/10 cases match their expectation** (verified, not assumed — see terminal output captured during the build session).
- Wrote `bench/README.md` documenting the layout, patch format/apply convention (`patch -p0`), and how to add a case.
- Noted deviation from the original case list in the build brief: case descriptions/exact bugs were adjusted from the initial plan where the first attempt didn't reproduce the intended failure (e.g. `compare.ts`'s array-handling had to be simplified so the `hard-shared-isplainobject` bug could actually manifest through the shared helper) — every case in this log reflects what was actually verified to fail, not the original plan.

**Planned next:** M2 — agent v1 end-to-end (reproduce → locate → patch → verify → commit loop, traced in neatlogs) against one easy case locally.

## Demo

### 2026-10-11 — M2: Agent v1 end-to-end
- **Model switch (deliberate, user-requested):** moved from Anthropic Claude to Google Gemini (`@google/genai`, model `gemini-3.8-flash` -- the API itself told us `gemini-2.5-flash` is retired and to use `gemini-3.8-flash`) for the agent's own LLM calls, to run on Gemini's free tier for the hackathon. Traced via `neatlogs/google-genai`'s `wrapGoogleGenAI`. Verified both the SDK's actual exports and the live API's model-availability error rather than assuming either.
- Built the tool-calling agent loop (`src/agent/loop.ts`) with 7 tools (`graph_search`, `graph_explain`, `read_file`, `apply_edit`, `run_tests`, `revert_last_edit`, `finish`), a system prompt enforcing the reproduce→locate→patch→verify cycle and the no-cheating rule, and per-run cost/attempt budget tracking (`src/agent/state.ts`, persisted to `runs/<id>/state.json` after every step).
- **Upgraded LOCATE and VERIFY to real Entire-graph commands** (stronger than the original plan): `entire graph search` for locating fix sites (ranked, with file:line + source), and `entire graph verify --record-baseline` / `--pre-edit-baseline` for an adjudicated PASS/REGRESSION/NO-EFFECT verdict against a pre-edit baseline, instead of hand-parsing test runner output.
- Anti-cheat guardrail (`src/verify.ts`, pulled forward from M3): rejects a claimed fix if the diff skips/deletes tests. A claimed "fixed" is NEVER trusted directly -- it's always re-verified with `entire graph verify` + the diff check before a commit is made.
- **Two real bugs found and fixed while getting this working (both are real recovery/debugging evidence, not staged):**
  1. vitest's default reporter embeds a nondeterministic duration ("1ms" vs "0ms") in each failing test's name and only names passing tests at file granularity -- this broke `entire graph verify`'s baseline diff (a 100%-unchanged tree was misreported as "4 REGRESSIONS" because the timing suffix differed between the baseline run and the re-run). Fixed by forcing `--reporter=verbose` onto the test command (detected via the target repo's own `package.json` script, since `testCmd` is usually just `"npm test"` and doesn't literally say "vitest").
  2. **Command injection**: `gitCommitAll` built the `git commit -m "..."` command via `execSync` on an interpolated string. The LLM's own commit-message summary contained markdown backticks (e.g. `` `src/capitalize.ts` ``), and `/bin/sh` executes backtick-quoted text as command substitution even inside double quotes -- the shell genuinely tried to run `src/capitalize.ts` and `capitalize` as commands on the first real run. Fixed by switching all of `src/tools/git.ts` to `execFileSync` with argument arrays (no shell involved, so no interpolation risk) instead of `execSync` with a built string.
  3. Added exponential backoff (`src/agent/loop.ts`) after hitting a real transient `503 UNAVAILABLE` from the Gemini API during testing.
- **Ran it end-to-end against `stringkit/easy-capitalize`:** graph_search found the bug (score 21.4 vs 9.4 for the next candidate) → read_file → apply_edit → run_tests → `entire graph verify` returned PASS (4 newly passing, 0 regressions) → committed. Full suite re-verified independently afterward: 36/36 passing. Cost: ~$0.014 (gemini-3.8-flash paid-tier equivalent; actual run was on the free tier). 5 attempts used of a 6-attempt budget.
- Added `--case <project>/<id>` convenience flag to the CLI (materializes a bench case into `runs/<run-id>/workspace` via the shared `bench/lib/prepare.ts` helper, extracted from `run-bench.ts` so both share one tested code path).

**Planned next:** M3 — formalize the recovery handlers already touched above (apply_edit-not-found retry, timeout handling, budget exhaustion -> draft report) and resume-from-state.json. Then M4 — run the full 10-case benchmark through the agent and record the "before" numbers.

# Greenlight — neatHack build log

## Project

**Name:** Greenlight
**One-sentence purpose:** An autonomous agent that turns a red CI run into a merged-ready pull request, with no human in the loop.
**Problem:** Engineers lose time triaging and fixing routine test failures; Greenlight handles the reproduce → locate → patch → verify → recover loop end to end.

## Team

- zoro (solo, so far)

## Stack

- TypeScript / Node.js 20+, Google Gemini (`@google/genai`, `gemini-3.8-flash`) for the agent's own LLM calls
- neatlogs (tracing) — TS SDK
- Entire (build checkpoints) + entire-graph (runtime code graph)
- cfo.ai (business plan)
- GitHub Actions + Octokit (real red-CI → PR demo)

## Build log

### 2026-10-11 — M0: Setup
- Repo initialized, public GitHub repo created under `ivedmohan`.
- Entire CLI 0.11.4 installed via Homebrew; `entire enable` + `entire login` pending (human step).
- Neatlogs API key wired into `.env` (gitignored); project ID `73ddd324-c4e6-48fd-8667-2db6335ae52d`.
- Project scaffolded: `src/` (agent, tools, tracing), `bench/`, `evidence/`.
- Noted doc discrepancies vs. the original build brief:
  - Entire checkpoints are git refs at `refs/entire/checkpoints/<shard>/<id>` (linked via `Entire-Checkpoint` commit trailer), not a `entire/checkpoints/v1` branch.
  - entire-graph's search command is `entire graph query "<text>"`, not `entire graph search`. Setup is `entire graph init-agents --repo .` then `entire graph index`.

- `entire login` completed (human step); `entire auth status` confirms logged in as `github:ivedmohan`, checkpoints syncing to `origin`.

### 2026-10-11 — M1: Benchmark repos
- Built two golden seed projects under `bench/repos/`:
  - `stringkit` — TS utility library (capitalize, slugify, truncate, sum/clamp, array helpers, deepEqual, merge, retryWithBackoff). 8 test files, 36/36 tests passing.
  - `tasks-api` — tiny Express CRUD API for tasks, tested with supertest. 1 test file, 13/13 tests passing.
- Seeded 10 bug cases under `bench/cases/<project>/<id>/` (a `bug.patch` unified diff + `meta.json` with the difficulty and the *observed*, not assumed, failing tests):
  - `easy-capitalize` (stringkit) — `slice(0)` vs `slice(1)` duplicates the first char.
  - `easy-clamp` (stringkit) — off-by-one at the max boundary.
  - `easy-sum` (stringkit) — reduce starts at 1 instead of 0.
  - `medium-slugify-shared-helper` (stringkit) — bug is in `internal/normalize.ts`, not `slugify.ts`.
  - `medium-retry-missing-await` (stringkit) — missing `await` breaks error handling in `retryWithBackoff`.
  - `hard-shared-isplainobject` (stringkit) — one shared-helper bug breaks two unrelated test files at once (`compare.test.ts` + `merge.test.ts`); fix must go in the shared helper.
  - `flaky-retry-backoff-explosion` (stringkit) — backoff formula explodes, causing genuine test **timeouts** (verified at `--testTimeout=3000`, all 3 tests time out), not just wrong assertions.
  - `easy-completed-filter` (tasks-api) — query-string boolean not coerced before filtering.
  - `medium-update-store-bug` (tasks-api) — `updateTask()` returns a non-persisted copy; route code is correct, bug is cross-file.
  - `hard-validate-partial-flag-ignored` (tasks-api) — shared validation ignores the `partial` flag, breaking PATCH while CREATE still needs the required-title check; fix must be conditional.
- Wrote `bench/run-bench.ts`: for every case, copies the golden project, applies its patch, runs the real test suite, and checks observed failing test files against `meta.json`. **Ran it: 10/10 cases match their expectation** (verified, not assumed — see terminal output captured during the build session).
- Wrote `bench/README.md` documenting the layout, patch format/apply convention (`patch -p0`), and how to add a case.
- Noted deviation from the original case list in the build brief: case descriptions/exact bugs were adjusted from the initial plan where the first attempt didn't reproduce the intended failure (e.g. `compare.ts`'s array-handling had to be simplified so the `hard-shared-isplainobject` bug could actually manifest through the shared helper) — every case in this log reflects what was actually verified to fail, not the original plan.

**Planned next:** M2 — agent v1 end-to-end (reproduce → locate → patch → verify → commit loop, traced in neatlogs) against one easy case locally.
